newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Fran damaged U.S. tobacco -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Fran damaged U.S. tobacco -- USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department said Monday that Hurricane Fran disrupted flue-cured tobacco harvesting and curing.
Damage to unharvested tobacco was total in some areas of the Coastal Plain of North Carolina, South Carolina and parts of Virginia, the department said.
Extensive power outages also caused spoilage of tobacco in the curing barns after the storm passed, USDA said in its monthly Tobacco Situation and Outlook Summary.
The total effect on the crop was undetermined, the report said.

Total supply of U.S.-grown tobacco for 1996/97 will likely be down from 1995/96. Carry-in stocks -- July 1 for flue-cured and cigar wrapper types and October 1 for other types -- were likely to decline five percent from a year earlier, and, considering hurricane damage, gains in production may not offset the decline.
Prior to the hurricane, tobacco production was forecast up 25 percent from the previous season because of higher acreage and yields, the report said.
